dek_candidates: What the DRHP discloses about A B Infrabuild Limited's business, offer, financials and risks — sourced to the filing, page by page.
A B Infrabuild Limited, an infrastructure and ready-mix concrete company concentrated on Mumbai and Western Railway, files for an SME IPO. Here is what the draft prospectus says.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild operates in two segments: infrastructure creation (railways, bridges, roads) and operating a ready-mix concrete plant at Kashimira, Thane.

Contracts are won through a public tender process: the client floats a tender, a pre-bid meeting is held, the contractor bids, and the job is awarded to the lowest bidder. The company then deposits a performance guarantee.

Major clients include Western Railways, Central Railways, Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation Ltd (MRVCL), Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM), and Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA).
Revenue is heavily concentrated: in Fiscal 2018, 57% of total revenue came from key customers, and as of the DRHP date, Western Railway alone accounted for 52% of the orders on hand.
The company uses the 'Box Pushing' technique in its projects and has invested in state-of-the-art machinery and quality control systems at its RMC facility.
Its order book is concentrated in Mumbai and Maharashtra, and the company describes itself as a 'major player in developing infrastructure in the city of Mumbai'.

beats.beat: Revenue from operations has declined from ₹9,021.12 lakhs in FY2015 to ₹6,053.05 lakhs in FY2018, a drop of about 33%.
Net profit after adjustments fell from ₹95.95 lakhs in FY2014 to a low of ₹15.86 lakhs in FY2017, but rebounded sharply to ₹314.66 lakhs in FY2018.
EBITDA (Profit Before Interest, Depreciation and Tax) has fluctuated: ₹784.46 lakhs (FY2014), ₹945.78 lakhs (FY2015), ₹783.31 lakhs (FY2016), ₹676.19 lakhs (FY2017), and ₹928.80 lakhs (FY2018).
Short-term borrowings have risen steadily from ₹3,082.27 lakhs in FY2014 to ₹3,537.35 lakhs in FY2018, while long-term borrowings declined from ₹586.63 lakhs to ₹133.09 lakhs over the same period.
Total assets grew from ₹7,062.34 lakhs (FY2014) to ₹8,232.15 lakhs (FY2018).
The company has reported negative cash flows in recent years, which it acknowledges as a risk that could affect operations.
Key ratios disclosed in the Basis for Issue Price: EPS for FY2018 is ₹12.39, NAV per share is ₹44.71, and RoNW is 28.14%.

beats.beat: The sole promoter is Amit Bholanath Mishra, who holds 74,95,476 equity shares, representing 90.949% of the pre-issue paid-up capital.
Other directors hold only 300 shares each: Bharat Kumar Parmar (Whole Time Director), Shree Prakash Singh (Whole Time Director), and Mukesh Pandey (Whole Time Director).
Key management personnel include Ms. Anchal Pachori (CFO, aged 28, CA) and Mr. Mohit Soni (Company Secretary, aged 26, ACS).
Hatim Sakerwala holds 9% of the equity shares as of the DRHP date.
Related-party transactions for FY2018 include loans taken from KMP/Board of Directors (₹68.4 lakhs), director remuneration (₹57.7 lakhs), and outstanding payables to related parties (₹324.3 lakhs).
Two companies promoted by Amit Mishra — Al-Noor Chickens Private Limited and A B Magma Automobiles Private Limited — were struck off by the Registrar of Companies in March 2016 due to non-operation.
No criminal cases or investigations have been filed against the directors, and none are on the RBI's list of willful defaulters.

beats.beat: The infrastructure sector in India is highly fragmented, working-capital intensive, and contributes about 8% to India's GDP (at constant prices).
India's construction market was valued at US$ 400 billion in 2015 and is projected to reach US$ 1 trillion by 2025, according to industry data cited in the DRHP.
Growth drivers include government programs such as the 100 Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT, Make in India, and eased FDI norms in 15 sectors including real estate and construction.
The logistics sector, a related segment, is expected to grow at a CAGR of 10.5% from US$ 160 billion in 2017 to US$ 215 billion by 2020.
Competition comes from both organized and unorganized players. The DRHP notes headwinds such as the slow pace of government projects, working capital crunches, and changes in government policies.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild Limited is an infrastructure construction and ready-mix concrete (RMC) company based in Mumbai, operating primarily on government contracts, especially from Indian Railways.
Its promoter, Amit Bholanath Mishra, holds 90.949% of the pre-issue equity — 74,95,476 shares out of a total pre-issue paid-up capital that will be diluted by the fresh issue.

The company is raising funds through a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares of ₹10 each at a price to be determined, with no offer-for-sale component. The lead manager is Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who A B Infrabuild is, what it does, and what it is raising on the SME Board.

beats.beat: The IPO consists entirely of a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares; there is no offer-for-sale, so all proceeds will go to the company.
The lead manager to the issue is Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited, and the registrar is Bigshare Services Private Limited.
The main object of the issue is to meet working capital requirements, for which the company has allocated ₹1,130 lakhs.
A portion of the proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes, the exact amount of which is not disclosed (shown as [●] in the DRHP).
The company has not appointed an independent agency for appraisal of the project, and no monitoring agency has been appointed; fund deployment will be monitored by the Audit Committee.

beats.beat: Customer concentration: 57% of FY2018 revenue came from key customers, and 52% of the order book is from Western Railway. Losing that relationship would severely impact revenue.
Negative cash flows: The company has experienced negative cash flow in recent years, which could strain working capital and operations.
Order book volatility: Contracts in the order book may be adjusted, cancelled, or suspended by clients, so the order book is not necessarily indicative of future revenue.

Related-party transactions and unsecured loans: The company had ₹405.02 lakhs in unsecured loans repayable on demand as of March 31, 2018, and has ongoing related-party dealings that could present conflicts.
Promoter's struck-off companies: Two companies promoted by Amit Mishra were struck off by the ROC for non-operation, raising governance concerns.
